title: What to watch at the open
text: After Friday's big drop, stock futures pointed higher overnight. Futures are early bets on where stocks will open. On Sunday evening, S&P 500 futures were up about 1.1% and Nasdaq 100 futures about 1.9%, so the tech heavy names that fell most on Friday could bounce first. A bounce after a hard week is common, but it does not mean the worry is over. This is also a short week: markets are closed Thursday for Thanksgiving and close early, at 1 pm, on Friday.

title: NVIDIA starts the week at its 52 week low
text: NVIDIA closed Friday at $125.53, less than 1% above its lowest price of the past year. A Reuters report says the SEC, the market's government referee, is studying how the company reports its money. The company is also still looking for a permanent CEO. Analysts' average price target slipped from about $276 to $269. Its risk score stays at 6.7, which is High.

title: A rate hike is expected in December
text: The Federal Reserve meets on December 8 and 9. Traders now see roughly a 95% chance it raises its key interest rate by a quarter of a percent, to a range of 4.00% to 4.25%. Higher rates make borrowing cost more, and that usually weighs on fast growing tech stocks. The 10 year Treasury yield averaged 5.13% in October, its highest level of the past year.

title: Eli Lilly keeps holding up
text: Eli Lilly fell only 0.3% on Friday and sits about 9% below its high of the year, while chip stocks fell 10% to 14%. Lilly also agreed to buy a small company working on a treatment for Huntington's disease, for up to $725 million. Health care companies often move differently from tech, which is one reason to own more than one kind of business.

title: Lesson 62: What is an acquisition?
text: An acquisition is when one company buys another company. The buyer gets the other company's products, ideas, workers and customers. Big companies do this to grow faster than they could by building everything themselves. For example, a drug company can buy a small lab that is working on a promising medicine. The words "up to" in a deal mean part of the money is only paid later if certain goals are reached, like a medicine passing its tests. Acquisitions can help a company, but they can also fail if the buyer pays too much or the new product does not work out.

text: Prices, beta, 52 week ranges and analyst targets come from Financial Modeling Prep and are Friday's closing values.
